title: KV allocation probe: contiguous-hint allocation and background coalescing
creator: Asha Patel
description: Investigation and implementation of a lightweight 'contiguous-hint' allocation mode for the KV token cache plus an opportunistic background coalescer. Goal: reduce fragmentation and peak GPU memory overhead under continuous batching workloads while preserving hit-rate and latency SLOs.
background: We observe recurring high fragmentation ratios on long-lived GPU pods that serve high-concurrency continuous-batching traffic. Fragmentation shows up as: (1) unexpectedly low usable capacity despite free bytes reported by the allocator, (2) elevated eviction churn and compaction frequency, and (3) transient OOMs during bursty rollout windows. Existing approaches (fine-grained slab packing + periodic full compaction) work but cause spikes in GPU activity and latency regressions. This ticket prototypes a lower-impact allocation strategy that biases hot prefixes into contiguous runs and performs incremental coalescing during low-util windows.
technical_design:
Approach summary:
- Allocation hint: expose a reserve_hint flag in the KV allocation API used by the runtime batcher and tokenizer to mark tokens that are likely to be hot (prefixes, system tokens, recurring prompts). When reserve_hint is set, allocator attempts to allocate from a contiguous run of slots aligned to an allocation-granularity (e.g., 64KB alignment) to minimize internal fragmentation and reduce scatter during GPU memcpy.
- Contiguous slab metadata: maintain a compact per-slab header (bitmask + free-run-length cache) that lets the allocator quickly find runs of N contiguous slots without scanning entire pool. The header is sized to 64 bytes per slab to keep metadata cacheable.
- Micro-coalescer: implement a background coroutine that runs opportunistic coalescing passes on slabs with high fragmentation score. It performs small, bounded copy-and-update operations (move up to M tokens per slab pass) to merge free holes; each move updates a lightweight indirection table to keep other components consistent during the window.
- Indirection-forwarding grace: during moves, reads check a two-entry per-token forwarding slot (old->new pointer) to maintain correctness without global locks. After a quiet epoch (no in-flight requests referencing old slot), forwarding entries are cleared.
- Batching integration: batcher emits reserve_hint for tokens that match frequent prefix fingerprints (maintained per-model). For ephemeral requests without hints, allocator uses default best-fit policy.
- Heuristics and thresholds: fragmentation_score = (free_hole_count * avg_hole_size) / slab_capacity. Triggers: coalescer runs when fragmentation_score > 0.12 and free_bytes_threshold < 8% of slab size. Relocation limit is 256 tokens per slab per minute to bound write amplification.
- Fallbacks: if contiguous allocation fails after N attempts, fall back to indirection-based insert into hot-pool (existing indirect mapping). A runtime flag controls gradual rollout.
- Memory & perf considerations: contiguous runs reduce scatter I/O and make GPU memcpy coalesced; micro-coalescing spreads throughput over time to avoid spikes. Expected metadata overhead ~0.1% of GPU memory for headers + forwarding table.
- Correctness: ensure checkpoint/load and snapshotting persist indirection and forwarding entries; add upgrade path to replay in-flight moves during restart.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce median per-pod KV fragmentation_ratio by >= 25% on continuous-batching benchmark (same load as production replay).
No regression in p95 generation latency > 5% compared to baseline for canary traffic.
Eviction churn (evictions/min) drops by >= 15% under steady-state load.
Background coalescer bounded: average GPU copy time per minute per pod < 10ms of additional GPU time (measured by executor timers).
Automated integration tests for checkpoint + in-flight relocation recovery added to CI with deterministic replay.
Observability: new dashboard panels for fragmentation_score, coalescer_moves/min, forwarding_entry_fill, contiguous_alloc_success_rate.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: lab prototype with synthetic microbench (unit tests + microbench harness) — validate invariants and memory overhead.
Phase 1 (canary): enable contiguous-hint on one canary pool (10% traffic, non-critical accounts) for two weeks; collect fragmentation and latency metrics.
Phase 2 (ramp): increase to 30% if canary stable for 7 days and acceptance criteria met. Monitor for cross-tenant interference.
Phase 3 (safe-default): flip allocator flag to allow reserve_hint but keep heuristics conservative for 90% roll; monitor for 14 days.
Phase 4: gradual default enablement and documentation + SDK flag to opt-in/out.
Rollback: immediate revert to existing allocator if eviction_rate or p95 latency regresses > 10% for 3 consecutive minutes.
risks: Relocation write-amplification: moves increase GPU memcpy and may increase thermal/GPU util spikes; mitigation: strict per-slab rate limits and backoff during high GPU load.
Forwarding indirection correctness: complexity during restarts/checkpoints; mitigation: extend snapshot to include forwarding table and validate with CI deterministic replay.
Cross-tenant noise: aggressive coalescing on shared pods could impact other tenants; mitigation: tenant-aware throttling and coalescer token-bucket per-tenant.
Heuristic tuning: mis-set thresholds could reduce effective capacity; mitigation: expose runtime knobs and A/B test ranges in canary.

Edge-case workloads: extremely high-churn short-lived tokens may not benefit and could be harmed; mitigation: only apply reserve_hint for tokens with a min-fingerprint-hit-rate over a sliding 1h window.
notes: Related tickets: ENG-314159 (ghost-slab prototype) - reuse slab header format; ENG-772413 (mosaic allocation heuristics) - coordinate heuristics and fingerprinting
